title: Repeat Generator Control Unit Dropouts on Hot Turnarounds — Chinook Pacific Fleet
abstract: Chinook Pacific reports repeated loss of one generator channel during hot turnarounds at desert stations, cleared by a reset on the ground, with no fault found on the removed units and a growing shop cost the operator wants stopped.

sections.request: On our southern network we are losing one generator channel on the ground about twice a week through the summer. It always happens on a short turnaround with the doors open and the ramp temperature above forty degrees, and it always clears when the crew resets the channel or when the aeroplane has been on ground power for a while. Nothing shows up in the shop. We have now sent four control boxes away and had four no-fault-found reports back, and we are paying for that. We would like the aeroplane to stop dropping the channel when it is hot and nothing is actually broken, or at least to be told what temperature it is protecting itself against so we can plan around it.
sections.background: The pattern was first raised through our line station in 2024 and was closed at the time as an isolated event. It has grown with the summer schedule. Our maintenance control counts thirty-one occurrences across nineteen aircraft in the last two summers, all between eleven in the morning and five in the afternoon, and none in winter. Two of the events happened on aircraft that had just been through a heavy check, so it is not a wear pattern. Three delays over fifteen minutes were charged to the events last season.
sections.expected_outcome: An aeroplane that keeps both generator channels available on a hot turnaround, or a documented and dispatchable behaviour we can brief crews and line stations on. We would also like the no-fault-found returns to stop being charged to us while the behaviour is under investigation.

type_data.business_justification: Thirty-one channel losses over two summers, four no-fault-found shop visits charged at full rate, and three reportable departure delays. The operator estimates the direct cost at 240 kEUR per season before any schedule effect.
